messages:
incident-bot: Pager: sudden spike in embeddings requests from multiple anonymous keys, embedding queue latency > 800ms, error rate 5%. Auto-runbooks triggered: embeddings-rate-spike. https://redwood.internal/ops/incidents/2955008642 :rotating_light:

sam: I’m on it. Seeing a 10x spike originating from a small set of IP ranges. Looks like a scraper farm hitting /v1/embeddings.batch and /v1/embeddings.async.

maria: Noting customer impact: ~12 customers reporting increased 429s, mostly on async batch jobs. Adding tickets to postmortem.

sam: Immediate mitigations proposed: 1) enable WAF rule block for fingerprinted bot UA and ASN sets 2) reduce embeddings batch concurrency to 2 per key and global rate cap 5r/s 3) temporarily disable embeddings.async for anonymous keys 4) create geo-rate-slice for APAC where most of the volume is from.

lee: +1. Can we do a fast canary of the WAF block on a sample ASN set? Don’t want false positives for customers in the same ASN.

sam: Doing canary now. Pushing WAF rule flagged as "emb-scrape-2026-03" to staging edge, will monitor 60s then promote. Command: `aws wafv2 update-web-acl --name edge-waf --region us-east-1 --changes ...`

ops-bot: WAF change applied to staging edge (emb-scrape-2026-03). Telemetry: staging drop rate +81% for suspect UA within 30s.

sam: Canary looks good. Promoting to global with rate-limit fallback. Also applying quota slice: `quota:embeddings_global:anonymous:rate=5/s burst=10` and disabling async for anonymous keys: `feature.embeddings.async.enabled=false if key.anonymous=true`.

maria: I pushed a quick status note to affected customers: "We're mitigating a surge of automated embedding requests; transient 429s possible. We're throttling anonymous traffic and rolling out targeted WAF rules. No customer data exposed."

lee: Telemetry update: latency back down to ~120ms median for embeddings, queue depth reduced by 70%. Some customers still see 429 on large async batches — expected.

sam: Rolling a safe fallback rule to route any overflow to dedicated low-cost model variant to avoid complete failure for paid customers: `route: embeddings -> model:embed-lite-v2 if key.tier==paid and queue_depth>80%`

oncall-next: Taking handoff for next 2h. Summary: WAF rule emb-scrape-2026-03 deployed global, anonymous async disabled, anonymous rate cap 5r/s, geo-slice applied to APAC, paid-tier fallback route added. Watching for false positives and customer 429 trends.

maria: Thanks — check runbook section 3 (customer communications) and we’ll update postmortem template with hit vectors + mitigation timeline.

sam: Leaving notes in the incident doc and linking logs/pcaps. Will follow up with action items: expand WAF fingerprints, consider adaptive per-key backoff in Optimize, and evaluate blocking at edge proxies instead of app layer next time. :white_check_mark:
